overview: Muun (Humanoid mammal) is native to Muunilinst and ranks among the most consequential species in galactic history. Muun bankers from Muunilinst lead the InterGalactic Banking Clan, financing both Republic and Separatist war machines during the Clone Wars.
history:
The Muun (humanoid mammal) trace their deepest roots to Muunilinst, where fossil beds, oral traditions, and surviving ruins suggest millennia of uninterrupted development. Muun evolutionary history on Muunilinst intertwines with humanoid mammal adaptation, local predator cycles, and early hyperspace contact logs preserved in both Jedi and Sith archives. Galactic surveyors first catalogued Muun populations during the expansion of the Old Republic, though local records often predate offworld contact by thousands of years. Across films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Ahsoka, KOTOR, KOTOR II, The Old Republic, and Sith Empire chronicles, Muun history is treated as foundational rather than peripheral.

In the Ancient Era and early Old Republic, Muun societies on Muunilinst established trade routes, planetary defense, and Force traditions that later empires would inherit or suppress. Ancient Muun polities negotiated with Rakatan remnants, Sith emissaries, and Core Founders; archaeological teams still uncover Muunilinst ruins that rewrite pre-Republic timelines. Archaeologists still debate how much of modern Muun identity was shaped by Rakatan influence, Infinite Empire collapse, and the long shadow of the Sith. High Republic archives mention Muun delegations, warriors, and artisans whose contributions were later rediscovered only through holocrons and battlefield inscriptions.

From the Clone Wars through the Imperial Era and into the New Republic, Muun diaspora communities appeared on every major trade lane and war front. Modern Muun diaspora appear in Clone Wars battlefronts, Rebels cells, Mandalorian guild halls, and Ahsoka-era investigations—often as the decisive local expert outsiders underestimated. Mandalorian-era intelligence briefings and Ahsoka-era reconstructions confirm that Muun networks remained active even when their homeworld fell under occupation or blockade. Sequel-era historians now treat Muun migration patterns as a map of galactic trauma and renewal, not mere demographic noise.

Muun fought in the galaxy's defining wars—not only as soldiers but as spies, healers, smugglers, and refugees whose choices shifted battle outcomes. Muun veterans fought in the Jedi Civil War (KOTOR), Sith Empire returns (TOR), Clone Wars sector campaigns, and the Galactic Civil War with tactics shaped by Muunilinst's geography. KOTOR and KOTOR II document Muun involvement in the Jedi Civil War, while TOR and Sith Empire materials show parallel struggles against the Eternal Empire and Dread Masters. Rebels and Clone Wars episodes repeatedly demonstrate that a single Muun leader can rally a sector or, conversely, expose a conspiracy that topples a fleet.
significance:
Biologically, the Muun display traits typical of humanoid mammal life adapted to Muunilinst's gravity, atmosphere, and seasonal extremes. Muun physiology—documented in Republic medical droids and Imperial biometrics—explains survival rates under occupation, labor extraction, and frontline service across eras. Medics note that Muun physiology interacts with cybernetics, clone templates, and Force healing in ways that are well documented in Republic medical journals. Geneticists argue that Muun resilience under occupation and exile explains much of their survival rate across the Rim and Unknown Regions.

Muun culture encodes memory through art, ritual, cuisine, and language dialects that survive even when homeworld cities are bombed flat. Muun rituals, language dialects, and art forms survived offworld commodification; cultural revival movements on Muunilinst accelerated after the Empire's collapse. Both Jedi and Sith sources acknowledge Muun spiritual practices, though each tradition interprets those practices through its own doctrine of attachment and power. Living Muun communities on Coruscant, Nar Shaddaa, and Ferrix-style industrial worlds prove that culture is portable when homeworld sovereignty is not.

The galactic impact of the Muun exceeds what population tables suggest: their merchants, admirals, crime lords, and senators rewrote trade law and fleet doctrine. Galactic historians cite Muun merchants, soldiers, Force users, and criminals as pivot points in treaties, fleet battles, and underworld realignments from the Old Republic to the Sequel Era. Historians credit Muun innovators with breakthroughs in hyperspace navigation, droid ethics debates, and post-Imperial reconciliation councils. Whether aligned with the Republic, the Separatists, the Rebellion, or independent Mandalorian clans, Muun choices remain reference points in every major era study.
